QEVA RECOVERY CORE 0.4
======================

PURPOSE
QEVA preserves explicit mathematical objects, their exact revision-pinned
logical dependencies, their provenance, and separate historical/corpus
relations.  This file is a low-complexity recovery description.  A future
custodian does not need this website, Python, JSON Schema, a database, or the
QEVA institution in order to interpret the archive.

FOUR LAYERS
1. LOGICAL ARCHIVE: definitions, axioms, statements, proofs, conjectures,
   counterexamples, algorithms, and frameworks.
2. HISTORICAL GRAPH: people, works, dates, discoveries, corrections,
   formalizations, and disputes.
3. CORPUS GRAPH: source records, identifiers, retrieval events, rights, raw
   fixity, normalization, and machine-extracted candidates.
4. VIEWS: website, maps, timelines, sandboxes, indexes, and future software.

The first three layers are data.  The fourth is replaceable software.

PERMANENT SEPARATIONS
  syntax                is not semantics
  derivability          is not model satisfaction
  citation              is not logical dependence
  co-occurrence         is not mechanism
  analogy               is not equivalence
  simulation            is not proof
  publication           is not truth
  popularity            is not importance
  web accessibility     is not redistribution permission

FOUNDATIONAL STANCE
QEVA does not claim that all mathematics has one uncontested absolute root.
It records a small shared metalanguage (distinction, object, expression,
statement, rule) and then exposes multiple explicit foundational branches,
including classical set-theoretic, constructive/type-theoretic, and
category-theoretic presentations.  A bridge between branches must name the
translation or interpretation that supports it.

IDENTITY
A stable logical object identifier is:
  qeva:1:sequence
An exact released revision is:
  qeva:1:sequence@2

The namespace number after qeva: is part of the identifier grammar, not a
protocol version.  Object kind is metadata and is not part of identity.
Every QEVA dependency, relation target, framework_ref, and supersedes link
uses an exact revision.  Released revision bytes never change.

OBJECT 0.2
The canonical object fields are documented by qeva-object.schema.json:
  qeva_version, id, revision, kind, title, summary, domains, context,
  assumptions, content, dependencies, relations, verification, provenance,
  supersedes, legacy_ids.

The schema is an interoperability aid.  CORE.txt remains readable without a
schema implementation.  Protocol 0.2 objects remain valid inside release 0.4.

PROOF AND TRUTH
  Gamma |-_{S} P    means a permitted finite S-derivation of P from Gamma.
  M |= P            means P is satisfied in model M under declared semantics.

Neither notation has a complete meaning until S or M and the language are
recoverable.  QEVA never stores one unlabeled Boolean named true.

VERIFICATION LEVELS
  unreviewed       recorded but not editorially qualified
  editorial        checked for clarity/coherence by an editor
  formal-proof     accompanied by a formal derivation artifact
  machine-checked  replayed by a named checker/kernel
  refuted          an exact claim has a counterexample or derivation of denial

A level describes performed checking.  It does not transfer automatically to
dependent objects.

QUALIFICATION ASSERTIONS
An object's verification field is a release-time summary.  Independent checks
also live as append-only qualification records.  Each names an exact subject,
dimension, outcome, method, artifact, asserter, date, and environment.  Thus an
editorial review, formal derivation, machine replay, computational experiment,
empirical replication, and refutation can coexist without rewriting the
mathematical object or collapsing unlike evidence into one score.

ENCODING
Text is UTF-8 without a byte-order mark.  Generated lines end with LF byte
0x0A.  JSON follows RFC 8259.  Canonical JSON for digests sorts keys
lexicographically, emits no insignificant whitespace, emits Unicode directly,
and appends one LF byte.  JSONL contains one complete object per line.

FIXITY
SHA-256 and SHA-512 manifests record byte fixity.  Hashes do not prove
authorship, mathematical truth, or timeless security.  Future releases may add
new algorithms but must preserve old manifests and released bytes.

MIRRORS AND MIGRATION
Anyone may copy the complete QEVA-native release.  A migration preserves the
source bytes, writes a new representation, documents the transformation, and
keeps both.  A successor may continue from any complete mirror but must not
impersonate an earlier release.

RECOVERY ORDER
1. Verify MANIFEST.sha256 and/or MANIFEST.sha512.
2. Read RELEASE.json and this CORE.txt.
3. Read archive/CATALOG.tsv for a low-complexity index.
4. Read archive/current.jsonl for current objects.
5. Read archive/all.jsonl for exact revision history.
6. Read corpus/source-registry.json before handling third-party material.
7. Use snapshot/QEVA-BAG as a portable BagIt-style recovery subset.

END QEVA RECOVERY CORE 0.4
